utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, good afternoon to you. Could you call the case, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-05-88-PT, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic and others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam. All right. So let's proceed. I take it that Miletic and Gvero are still on provisional release, so I will address the others. Mr. Popovic, Vujadin, can you follow the proceedings in our own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Mr. Ljubisa Beara, can you follow the proceedings in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The microphones of the accused are not switched on. We actually cannot hear the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you for pointing that out to me. Please make sure that when you answer, when you reply, that you have your microphone switched on. Thank you. However, just for the record, I did hear the witness confirm that he can follow the proceedings in his own language. Drago Nikolic, can you follow the proceedings in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ljubomir Borovcanin, can you follow the proceedings in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BOROVCANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can follow it in my own language, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Pandurevic, can you follow the proceedings in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PANDUREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Mr. Trbic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED TRBIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can. Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So let's go to the presentation. For the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Peter McCloskey for the Prosecutor, and with me are, well, faces that are familiar and will become more familiar, Janet Stewart, our case manager; Antoinette Issa; and Nelson Thayer; and also with us today are Melina de la Garza and Sara Murphy with our legal staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see that you're striving towards achieving equality of arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. For Vujadin Popovic, Zoran Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Zivanovic, and good afternoon to you. For accused Beara.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: May it please Your Honour. Christopher Meek, co-counsel Nebojsa Mrkic for the accused Beara.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's the position of Mr. -- you have been appointed in the position.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have been -- you have been very simply approved or appointed as co-counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And what is Mr. Mrkic's position?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. Mrkic is a legal assistant from Belgrade, and lead counsel, Mr. Ostojic, could not make it, and he requested that Mr. Mrkic sit in on this hearing. I asked before the hearing if it would be appropriate, and to ask Your Honour, and I'd happily fill out any forms to allow Mr. Mrkic to sit in this Status Conference today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but has he been appointed as legal assistant?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Legal assistant, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: By the Registrar?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: That's my understanding, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. If that is the case, I won't question it any further.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Meek. And appearances for Drago Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Jelena Nikolic. Together with my colleague, Mr. Stephane Bourgon, we are representing Mr. Drago Nikolic in this case. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam, and good afternoon to you. Appearances for Ljubomir Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Aleksandar Lazarevic, and here by my side is Mr. Miodrag Stojanovic. We will represent Mr. Borovcanin's Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Lazarevic, and good afternoon to you and to your colleague. Appearances for Miletic, Radivoje.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Natacha Ivanovic, and I represent Radivoje Miletic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam. Appearances for -- and good afternoon to you. Appearances for Milan Gvero.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Krgovic, and good afternoon to you. Appearances for Vinko Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Peter Haynes, Your Honour, and Djordje Sarapa. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Haynes, and good afternoon to you, too, and to your colleague. Appearances for Milorad Trbic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROHAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Colleen Rohan for Mr. Trbic, and with me is my legal assistant Marina Akinova [phoen]. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Rohan. Good afternoon to you and your colleague. So I appeal for the cooperation of everyone. It's not going to be an easy Status Conference. There are many of us and everyone will have a little bit to say. So if we cooperate, we'll try to bring this Status Conference to an end successfully and within the shortest time possible. The last Status Conference, as you will all recall, those of you who were here, took place on the 10th of November of last year. I, as Pre-Trial Judge, had originally scheduled another Status Conference, the next Status conference, to be held on Tuesday, the 7th of March of this year. However, there were some developments, as a result of which I felt duty-bound not to hold that Status Conference on the scheduled day and appointed today as an alternative. The rescheduling was announced by means of an order that I signed on the 2nd of March, and the reason given, and I can assure you, consisted of unforeseen, very valid and justified reasons. For the sake of the public that follow these proceedings, may I just point out that Status Conferences are held pursuant to Rule 65 bis, and the main purpose of the Status Conference is to organise exchanges between the parties with a view to ensuring an expeditious preparation for trial and, in addition, to give the opportunity to every Accused to come and face-to-face with the Pre-Trial Judge, where issues relating to their mental and/or physical conditions as well as to their state of detention may be freely discussed. In preparation for this Status Conference, I asked my Senior Legal Officer to hold two 65 ter meetings. One was held just prior, the 3rd March date, although both Mr. Von Hebel and myself knew at the time that the Status Conference will not follow the day after. And the other one -- the first one took place on the 6th of March, to be precise, and the second one took place yesterday, on the 3rd of April. Mr. Von Hebel has duly informed me of everything that was discussed during these two 65 ter meetings, made notes of same, and I will be referring to some of these matters as we go along today. I will start first with what appears to be outstanding motions, and although in number they seem to be -- they appear to be quite a number, in reality there is much in common with plenty of them, with a lot of them, and I will explain to you how I propose to be dealing, with the utmost of judicial economy. You will recall that on the 11th of November of last year, the Prosecution filed a notice of filing a consolidated amended indictment which contained the text of the joint amended indictment against all accused in the present case. I then issued an order called -- on the 7th of December, 2005, and further to it, all accused were called upon to file preliminary motions in relation to or against the form of the consolidated amended indictment before the 9th of January of this year. All accused except you, Mr. Beara, did so. The Prosecution then filed a consolidated response on the 23rd of January of this year, and in the wake of this consolidated response, we had a number of accused filing a reply in return shortly afterwards. Then came the 22nd of March of this year. We are talking of very recently. And on the 22nd of March, the Prosecution filed a proposed amendment to the indictment in relation to one of the accused only, that is you, Mr. Borovcanin. On then the 29th of March, 2006, that's just barely over a week ago, the Prosecution then filed a motion to amend the indictment relating to the 22nd March 2006 Appeals Chamber decision or judgement in the case of Stakic. This motion aims at deleting from the consolidated amended indictment all references to the concept of direct and/or indirect co-perpetration, and to insert instead references to two forms of joint criminal enterprise; namely, the joint criminal enterprise with agreement and joint criminal enterprise with common purpose. Then I will just mention them, I have not had time to go through them because they arrived on my desk today while I was presiding over another case, but I have received today confirmation from the Registry of your appointment as co-counsel, Mr. Meek. I have Prosecution consolidated response to General Miletic's motion for access to confidential materials in the Perisic case and to rejoin the motions of Milan Gvero, Ljubomir Borovcanain, Drago Nikolic, and Vinko Pandurevic. These are tied already to some of the motions that we have. I also received today Vinko Pandurevic's Defence notification on joining the motion of General Gvero for access, confidential information in the Milosevic case. Again, that is connected to an existing -- another motion from General Gvero for access, confidential information in the Milosevic case. That goes with the other. And, of course, these matters will need to be addressed as I prepare the decisions on the outstanding motions. However, I wish to make it clear that I don't think it is the right moment now to enter into any debate on all the motions relating to the form of the indictment. There are several, as you all know. It is my intention, instead, to issue later on today in the course of this Status Conference a further oral order for the filing of responses and replies in order to allow me and the Trial Chamber seized with this case to take -- to come out with one consolidated decision on all pending motions on the indictment. We have been working very hard on this, but, of course, until the Appeals Chamber decision in the Stakic case we had even a particular motion dealing with co-perpetratorship, so we have done a lot of work, I won't say for nothing, but which kept us from concluding on other issues which now have to be concluded, but I can assure you that the matters, all outstanding matters are being attended to. This oral order that I will give within a couple of minutes will provide also a decision on the response filed by counsel for accused Gvero in relation to the amendment of the indictment on the 30th of March, 2006, which I have here with me in case we need to refer to it, and the motion filed by accused Borovcanin on the 31st of March just a few days ago for an extension of time. I emphasise that this oral order that I'm going to give shortly aims at getting the responses in from the parties, from all the parties, at the same time, on the same -- on both the issue under Rule 50, that is as to whether the Prosecution will be granted leave to amend the indictment, and also the substantive comments pursuant to Rule 72 on any alleged shortcomings in the formulation of the proposed amended indictment. So I'm trying to kill as many birds as possible with one stone, and I count on the cooperation of everyone. Having said this, I'm now going to proceed with my oral order. I, Carmel Agius, as Presiding Judge in this case, and in these pre-trial proceedings, having noted all the filings up until now on the form of the consolidated amended indictment filed by the Prosecution on the 11th of November, 2005, considering that judicial economy, amongst other considerations, dictates that the Trial Chamber takes one consolidated decision, not only in relation to all filings relating to the consolidated amended indictment itself but also to all additional and further submissions that I am hereby ordering and referring to in relation to the proposed amendments to -- the Prosecution's proposed amendments in their filings of the 22nd and 29th March, pursuant to Rules 50, 72, 126 bis and 127, I hereby order that, first, all accused will each file a consolidated response to the Prosecution's motion to amend the indictment relating to the 22nd March 2006 Appeals Chamber judgement in the case of Stakic filed on the 29th of March and the accused Borovcanin will also file a response to the Prosecution motion to amend the indictment relating to Ljubomir Borovcanin filed on the 22nd of March before or by Wednesday, the 12th of April, 2006, relating to the issue of amendment pursuant to Rule 50(A)(i)(c) and relating to any alleged defects in the form of the proposed amendments pursuant to Rule 72. Second, the Prosecution will file, if it so wishes, one consolidated reply to the Defence responses by Wednesday, 19th of April 2006. It is hoped that after that, the Chamber will then be in a position to issue one consolidated decision which will cover all previous issues and submissions that I referred to, plus the new ones following the motion by accused Borovcanin and also the motion by the Prosecution. There is a motion pending from accused Pandurevic relating to a renewed request for provisional release filed on the 30th of January, 2006. Now, on this, I am in discussions with the other two Judges in my Chamber, and we will be able to take a decision on this motion in due course. The same applies to similar almost identical motion filed by accused Borovcanin. We are discussing this, and we should be able to take a decision quite soon. Then accused Miletic, on the 21st of March 2006, requested a -- filed a motion requesting a translation of the pre-trial brief of the Prosecution into Serbo-Croat, and the time for the accused after the translation -- after translation has been provided to submit the pre-trial brief. There are several other co-accused that have joined in with this motion. I don't need to repeat every single one of them. This is being considered. It has reached a very advanced stage of elaboration. It's being drafted actually, and I assume that we should be in a position to decide it pretty soon. Finally, there is another motion by accused Miletic filed very recently, on the 28th of March of, 2005 [sic], requesting first a translation into B/C/S of two other motions that the Prosecution has announced to file; namely, one being or relating to adjudicated facts, and the other relating to the admission of witness statements pursuant to Rule 92 bis, and secondly, Mr. Miletic is also asking for time for the accused after the translation has been provided to submit their responses. Again, even if relation to this motion of Miletic, of the 28th of March, several other co-accused have joined in. I don't need to repeat the names. Again, this is also being dealt with and more or less it has reached the same stage as the previous one. It was more or less the same principle is more or less involved, and we hope that when we hand down the decision on the 21st March motion we will be able to hand down our decision on the 28th March motion too, unless I decide to combine them together in one decision, which is very likely what I will opt for. But I still am in the process of thinking about it, because there are some slight differences. All right. Before I move on to the next section, are there any comments from any of you on what I have stated so far before I move on to disclosure matters? I see none. So I come to disclosure matters. I am fully aware of the debate or exchange of discussions that took place during the two 65 ter meetings that I referred to earlier, which Mr. Von Hebel provided, and I am only going to dwell on those issues relating to disclosure where I think I either need some updating or some kind of information from you. First relates to disclosure under Rule 66(A)(ii). I am informed that roughly there are about 20 to 25 additional witness statements that are being prepared, and this is further to the forensic experts and 92 bis witnesses, and Mr. Von Hebel was more or less assured or given an indication by you, Mr. McCloskey that disclosure in this category will be completed by mid-April. I would like to have a formal confirmation from you that this is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. We fully intend to try, and it's just a matter of transcriptions and reports. We are very close to meeting that. We keep struggling and trying to take resources from the Krajisnik team, so if you have any pull with the Krajisnik judges that would be helpful. But it's a matter of resources and we are getting close, so I think we will be able to meet that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'll try to give a hand, Mr. McCloskey, but of course it doesn't depend much on me. I know how that Trial Chamber is working at full speed, and I know how limited our resources are but I will try to give a hand. All right. Are there any comments from the Defence side on Rule 66(A)(ii) disclosure, only on that category of disclosure or type of disclosure? I see none. I feel a little bit handicapped by this column here that hides Mr. Lazarevic, his colleague. Ms. Rohan and her legal assistant, I can barely see you. So if you need to attract my attention, please keep that in mind because it's not easy. I mean, I can't see you. So Rule 68 disclosure. Again, I'll be very specific here. I am informed that during the 65 ter meetings or conference of the 6th of March there were discussions between the parties on the issue of the use of the EDS system and the possibility of providing material to the Defence by CD-ROM because of the well known deficiencies in the EDS system. I am now informed, and please I would be happy to have a confirmation of this, that during yesterday's 65 ter conference, the parties informed my Senior Legal Officer that the Prosecution will be in a position to provide all 66 and 68 -- Rule 66 and 68 material on an external hard disk to the Defence so that they can have easy access to all core documentations for the trial. Do you confirm that, Mr. McCloskey? And do you confirm -- are you happy with that, members of the Defence teams?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. There has been a recent agreement to be able to provide a large amount of material directly on a hard disk, which I think is close to happening. It's not absolutely everything. There are still some collections that are in the EDS, but I think a good part of the collections are able to be just put on a hard drive and that's something that I'm confident will happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Any differing or -- opinions or remarks or comments? None? From the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. ROHAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, behind the pole.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Rohan.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROHAN
utterances.text: The Office of the Prosecutor has been extremely cooperative in working this out with the Defence. Still I think it might be useful if we would have some sense of the date when this might happen. If that's some information that you have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Ms. Rohan. Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Internally we are striving for 5 May, but Ms. Stewart tells me hopefully individual laptops by the end of the week. So everyone has been working hard on all this, Your Honour, and just to let you know, the Defence and the Prosecution, when up eight Defence counsels and a Prosecution that aren't saying anything in response to these questions, that's a reflection that everyone has been working very hard on these issues, just to let you know that, that there is a -- that the value of that silence is hard to put a price on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And I am -- enjoin you -- don't take this by any way of criticism, I am not criticising, but I enjoin you to chase this matter up to the best of your ability. Otherwise you have the complete trust of the Trial Chamber. I would like you to keep in mind also the need to bring the pre-trial proceedings to an end as quickly as we can, so that we can then start the trial at the first opportunity. So let's go into private session for a while because I need to discuss something in private session with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We are in open session. I am going to get very soon to the crucial part of today's Status Conference, and that's the entering of pleas. But before I do that, I am just going to try and briefly recapitulate the salient points that has brought us to this. I stated earlier that on the 11th of November of last year the Prosecution filed its consolidated amended indictment against all accused in the present joint case. This was in the wake of the decision given by Trial Chamber III of which I formed part, joining all the present accused together in one case. The indictment has been translated into B/C/S, and according to the information that I have available, made -- given to the accused, who very soon will be asked to enter their plea. In the meantime, as I stated earlier on, and I'm stating it again because I want to make one thing clear. In the meantime, as recently as the 22nd of this month, that is, the same day the appeals trial chamber handed down their appeal judgement in the Stakic case, the Prosecution filed a motion that -- relating only to accused Borovcanin seeking to further amend the consolidated amended indictment. And then exactly a week later, again once more in the wake of the Stakic appeal decision, judgement, Prosecution filed another motion to which I have referred already, again seeking to further amend the consolidated amended indictment, removing the concept of co-perpetratorship, co-perpetration and substituting therefore the question of joint criminal enterprise in its two forms. However, these amendments are at the moment still subject to Rule 50 -- to the Rule 50 procedure, and parties will need to be heard on this first as has been indicated above. In other words, it's premature to take into consideration these two motions or the contents of, substance of these two motions for the purpose of the exercise that we have today. So for all clarity, the pleadings that I am going to seek to obtain from the accused today, or from some of the accused today, will be against the indictment that was contained and as is contained in the OTP motion of the 11th November 2005, to which I have been referring as the consolidated amended indictment. Of course, if the litigation about these motions and further proposed amendment lead to further new charges against the accused, a further new pleading will, of course, become necessary once a decision is made and it becomes final. So that's the position. Because of this, I will be explaining, because I want to go to bed tonight with my conscience as quiet and as serene as possible, I will be explaining to each one of the accused the difference that there is between the original indictment and the consolidated amended indictment. And then each one will be asked to plead guilty or not guilty to the count, to the full count. I will be approaching the accuseds one by one to -- and ask them how they wish to plead, and I also wish to make sure of the following before I proceed. You would have noticed earlier on I said, "I am informed that not only has the consolidated amended indictment been translated into B/C/S but that you have each received a copy of it in your own language." If any one of you has not received the consolidated amended indictment in your own language, please stand up and speak up. So I take it that you have all. I also wish to know whether you have read this indictment. Is there anyone of you who has not read this indictment, the consolidated amended indictment? If there is, please speak up. Also it is my duty -- yes, I see Madam -- I'm sorry, I didn't see you before.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm very sorry, Mr. President. Excuse me for interrupting you. I wanted to say there was a third proposed amendment of the indictment attached to the response by the Prosecutor of the 23rd of January. I would like to say a few words about this, but you might wish to finish the pleadings first and then I could have the floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. I know about that. Thank you, Madam Fauveau. Let me finish with this exercise and then of course you will--

utterances.speaker: MS. FAVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So the Rules and the Statute also impose on me the responsibility to make sure that you fully understand the indictment and the nature of the charges that are brought against you in it. Is there any one of you that does not understand the indictment or the nature of the charges that have been brought against you and to which you will be pleading very soon? I see no reaction from the six co-accused. Next thing I would like to know, I know that this matter was more or less dealt with yesterday during the 65 ter meeting, but for reasons of my own, I want a confirmation from each one of you as to whether you would like the consolidated amended indictment to be read out in full here or whether you are waiving this right that you have. The right exists. If any one of you asks that we read out the consolidated amended indictment in full, we are duty-bound to do it, but this is a right that you can renounce to. Is there any one of you who would like me to read out the entire consolidated amended indictment? All right. Registrar, please enter into the records that none of the accused has expressed -- so I take it that you are waiving this right. The only conclusion I can draw is that one, and if you don't agree that this is the conclusion, please speak up now. So the consolidated amended indictment will not be read out or will be taken as read. Yes, Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. The Prosecutor filed three proposed amendments: One on the 23rd of January, 2006; the other one on the 22nd of March; and the last one in date was on the 29th of March. They are cumulative in nature, I believe. The problem the Defence now face, they have to provide a consolidated response, and they have to know exactly what are the amendments. I'm asking hereby the Prosecutor to file a consolidated proposal for the amendments. I'm not asking for postponement of the time or the dates, but I'd like to have this proposal by the end of the working day on Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's your reaction to that, Mr. McCloskey? Given that we will be proceeding today with what we have, that's based on the consolidated, 11th November consolidated amended indictment, the last two motions, 22nd and 29th of March, particularly the 29th of March one, will have to be dealt with subsequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe our motions speak for themselves. They are relatively clear, and if there is some confusion or some help I can -- we can speak with Ms. Fauveau outside of court, but I don't see the point in reshuffling everything to send it out again. It's there as we meant to file it, and I think it's clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, point taken. And if you need the Trial Chamber to deal with this specifically, Ms. Fauveau, please come forward with an ad hoc motion and we will decide accordingly. The problem that will arise definitely is substituting co-perpetratorship with joint criminal enterprise, are we talking of new charges, what are we talking about? Will there be the need for further plea and so on and so forth? Same applies to the Borovcanin measure. Anyway, I don't want to prejudice the Trial Chamber's position on this because this is a decision if asked -- if I am asked to take this decision, it will be in consultation with the other two Judges, so I cannot make a pronouncement myself on this. But in any case, we are going to proceed -- yes, Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the first proposed amendment filed on the 23rd of January had to do with Counts 4 and 5, and it had to do with the language of the two counts. Of course, General Miletic's Defence is not against the amendments. But the problem is that in the latest proposed amendment, that of the 29th of March, you don't have the new Counts 4 and 5. Therefore, we find it rather hard to meet this new mode of liability, or new mode of JCE, if the language of Counts 4 and 5 is not clearly defined. So I understood yesterday that the Prosecutor is of the view that all these changes add up, but I don't think it's up to the Defence to try and find in one proposal, one specific paragraph, and another paragraph and another. We should have a clear language for the indictment and we should also have it in the language of the accused if we want to be able to answer. We should at least have one clear proposal in one single text in order to provide a proper answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Faveau. My position doesn't change on this because it's not fit and proper for me to give an indication as to what I think, since this is obviously a matter that has to be dealt with by the Trial Chamber in its collegial format. So I'm going to deal with you one by one. Mr. Popovic, could you please stand up? Mr. Popovic, before I ask you to enter your plea, I wish to point out that if you prefer not to enter a plea of guilty or not guilty, in other words, if you remain passive and do nothing, I am bound by the Statute and the Rules to enter a plea of not guilty on your behalf. That's the position. So there is no way you can prejudice yourself by not entering a plea. I will point out first and foremost to you the difference between the initial indictment against you and the consolidated amended indictment. When I say the initial indictment, I mean that indictment which -- with which you were confronted when you first appeared before this Tribunal. You know that after that there was the joinder and then the consolidated amended indictment. Now in the first indictment, in the initial indictment, you were charged under Counts 1(a) and (b) with genocide or, in the alternative, complicity to commit genocide. The charge of complicity of genocide has now been removed from the indictment in order to avoid redundancy with the mode of liability of aiding and abetting under Article 7(1) of the Statute. There is, however, now a new Count 2 in the consolidated amended indictment that charges you with something akin but different and charges you with conspiracy to commit genocide. Also, in the initial indictment, you were charged with inhumane acts, consisting in the forcible transfer of the Bosnian Muslim population from the Srebrenica enclave and persecutions, including the forcible transfer of Bosnian Muslims from the Srebrenica enclave. You see the similarity or the common denominator in these two charges in the initial indictment. In the consolidated indictment, the charge of forcible transfer of Bosnian Muslims from the Srebrenica enclave, the charge of forceable transfer, not only applies to women and children but has been extended to include the forced bussing of men who were separated allegedly -- allegedly separated at Potocari or captured or having surrendered from the column of peoples fleeing the Srebrenica enclave up to the Zvornik area where they, according to the Prosecution, were ultimately captured and executed. In addition, the consolidated amended indictment charges the forcible transfer of the Bosnian Muslim population from the Zepa enclave, which wasn't before, including the deportation of men from Zepa. The charge of persecutions has also been extended in the consolidated amended indictment accordingly and the charge of deportation has been added. You see I've tried to explain to you how the indictment has changed from what it was to what it is now. What I'm going to do now, Mr. Popovic, and I invite the other co-accused to follow exactly what I'm doing, because this is what I'm going to do with each one of you later on, is I'm going to go through the charges one by one, as they are now in the consolidated amended indictment, and then I will ask you whether you wish to plead, and if you wish to plead, whether you wish to plead guilty or not guilty to each of these counts separately. Your answer should be either guilty or not guilty. I start with Count 1. Count 1 charges you with genocide punishable under Articles 4(3)(a) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. That is you are being charged with individual criminal responsibility for genocide. How do you wish to plead to this first count of genocide? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The accused pleads not guilty. Count 2 charges you with conspiracy to commit genocide punishable under Articles 4(3)(b) and Article 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Again you're charged with individual criminal responsibility here. How do you wish to plead to this second count; namely of conspiracy to commit genocide? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The accused pleads not guilty. Count 3 charges you with extermination, this being a crime against humanity punishable under Articles 5(b) and 7(1) of the Statute, again individual criminal responsibility. How do you wish to plead to this third count of extermination? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The accused pleads -- enters a plea of not guilty to the third count. Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise, Your Honour, for this, but the transcript shows that the accused Borovcanin is entering his plea instead of accused Popovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I thank you for pointing that out. I think that needs to be taken care of in the transcript. Mr. Borovcanin, you will still have a chance to enter your plea freely, and Mr. Popovic will not have the right to represent you. I can assure you of that. So we come -- so for the record, I just make it clear that what has been pointed out by Mr. Lazarevic is absolutely correct. The transcript should show accused Popovic and not Borovcanin. Count 4 charges you with murder, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(a) and Article 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you wish to plead to this Count 4, murder and -- count of murder?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Not guilty. Count 5 charges you with murder, this time being a violation of the laws or customs of war. Again, you're being charged under Article 3 and Article 7(1) of the Statute. How do you wish to plead? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Count 6 charges you with persecutions on political, racial and religious grounds, a crime against humanity. And these persecutions include murder, cruel and inhumane treatment, terrorising the civilian population, destruction of personal property and forcible transfer, all punishable under Articles 5(h) and 7(1) of the Statute of this Tribunal. How do you wish to plead to this sixth count consisting of persecutions?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Not guilty. Count 7 charges you with inhumane acts consisting in forcible transfer, a crime against humanity, punishable under 5 -- Articles 5(1) and 7(l) [sic] of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you wish to plead to this seventh count? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Popovic. We come to Count 8, which charges you with deportation. I've already explained how this has come in, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(d) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you wish to plead? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I ask the Registrar to put on record therefore that accused Mr. Popovic has pleaded not guilty to all the eight counts brought against him in the consolidated amended indictment. Mr. Popovic, I thank you so much. Please take a seat. And I now ask Mr. Beara to -- you can remain seated for the time being. I will ask you to stand up later. You are in a somewhat slightly different position. Following the consolidated amended indictment. Before I ask you to enter your plea, I will explain the difference that exists between the previous -- what I call the previous indictments. What I need to tell you is that in the amended indictment, you were charged with inhumane acts, namely forcible transfer and persecutions, including the forcible transfer of the Bosnian Muslim population from Srebrenica by means of the forced bussing of the women and children -- of women and children, to Bosnian Muslim-controlled territory, and the forced bussing of men separated at Potocari or captured or having surrendered from the column of people fleeing the Srebrenica enclave up to Zvornik area where, according to the Prosecution, they were captured and ultimately executed. In the consolidated amended indictment, the charge of forcible transfer has been extended to include also the forcible transfer of the Bosnian Muslim population from the Zepa enclave, which also includes the deportation of the men from Zepa. The charge of persecutions has also been extended in your case, in the consolidated amended indictment accordingly, and the charge of deportation has been added. So I now ask you to stand up and we'll go through the same procedure. Have you understood how your situation has changed?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BEARA
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much again I will be asking you whether you plead guilty or not guilty, and please restrict your answer to guilty or not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have problems hearing the accused. He is simply too far from the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Beara, the interpreters are telling me that you are too tall, and they can't -- and we can't -- no, it's okay. I mean, I will -- just raise your voice, the volume of your voice and they should be able to hear you. Are you hearing him now? Can you say something, please?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BEARA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, we can, but it is not as loud as it should be. This is better now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So Count 1, Mr. Beara, charges you with genocide which is punishable under Articles 4(3)(a) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. When I say 7(1), it means that you've been charged individually, in your own individual capacity, individual criminal responsibility. How do you wish it plead to this first count of genocide? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BEARA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Count 2 charges you with conspiracy to commit genocide punishable under Articles 4(3)(b) and 7(1) of the Statute. How do you wish to plead to there second count? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BEARA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Count 3 charges you with extermination, a charge that you had already, punishable under Article 5(b) and Article 7(1) of the Statute. How do you wish to plead to this third count of extermination? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BEARA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Count 4 charges you with murder, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(a) and Article 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you wish to plead to this fourth count of murder as a crime against humanity? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BEARA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Count 5 charges you again with murder but this time being a violation of the laws or customs of war, which is punishable under Article 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you wish to plead to this fifth count of murder?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BEARA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Count 6 charges you with persecutions on political, racial and religious grounds, that is being a crime against humanity, and which includes murder, cruel and inhumane treatment, terrorising the civilian population, destruction of personal property and forcible transfer punishable under Articles 5(h) and 7(1) of the Statute. How do you wish to plead? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BEARA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Count 7 charges you with inhumane acts, forcible transfer being a crime against humanity punishable under Articles 5(i) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you wish to plead? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BEARA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And finally Count 8 charges you with deportation, being a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(d) and 7(1) of the Statute. How do you wish to plead? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BEARA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Beara. You may sit down. And, Madam Registrar, could you please enter in the records of this case that accused Beara entered a plea of not guilty to all eight counts brought against him in the consolidated amended indictment. I now call on Drago Nikolic to pay attention. You may remain seated for the time being. I'll explain to you the differences between the initial indictment and the consolidated amended indictment. In the initial indictment, you were charged under Counts 1(a) and (b) with genocide or, in the alternative, with complicity to commit genocide, very similar to what your colleague Popovic was charged with. The charge of complicity of -- in genocide has now been removed from the indictment in order to avoid redundancy with the mode of liability of aiding and abetting under Article 7(1) of the Statute, but there is now a new Count 2 which charges you with conspiracy to commit genocide, and this is what you will be asked to enter a plea on. Also in the initial indictment you were charged with persecutions, not explicitly including forcible transfer, and you were not charged with forcible transfer as a separate count. The consolidated amended indictment, however, charges you with persecutions which include the forcible transfer of Bosnian Muslim population from Srebrenica and Zepa, which also includes the deportation of men from Zepa. It charges you accordingly with forcible transfer and deportation. More or less the same as I explained in the case of co-accused Popovic. So please stand up now, and we'll go through the eight counts, and I will be asking you how you wish to plead to each one of these eight counts. Count 1 charges you with genocide punishable under Article 5, 4(3)(a) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. When I say 7(1), I mean individual criminal responsibility. How do you wish to plead to this Count 1 of genocide? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Count 2 charges you with conspiracy to commit genocide, punishable under Articles 4(3)(b) and 7(1) of the Statute. How do you wish to plead? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Count 3 charges you with extermination, this being a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(b) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you wish to plead? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Count 4 charges you with murder, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(a) and 7(1) of the Statute. What's your plea? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Count 5 also charges you with murder, however this being a violation of the laws or customs of war punishable under Article 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you wish to plead to this Count 5 of murder? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Count 6 charges you with persecutions on political, racial and religious grounds, a crime against humanity, which includes murder, cruel and inhumane treatment, terrorising the civilian population, destruction of personal property and forcible transfer punishable under Articles 5(h) and 7(1) of the Statute of this Tribunal. How do you wish to plead to this sixth count of persecutions? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, not guilty. And Count 7 charges you with inhumane acts, being forcible transfer, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(i) and 7(1) of the Statute of this Tribunal. How do you wish to plead to this seventh count? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Count 8 charges you with deportation, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(d) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you wish to plead to this eighth and final count of deportation? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I thank you, Mr. Nikolic. You may sit down. And, Madam Registrar, could you kindly put on record that accused Nikolic entered a plea of not guilty to each of the eight counts brought against him in the consolidated amended indictment. Thank you. Ljubomir Borovcanin, please follow what I am going to inform you now. Yours is a little bit more extensive than that of the others. And then we will go through the usual procedure. In the initial indictment you were charged with complicity to commit genocide under Articles 4(3)(e), 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute. When I say 7(3), it's command and control, superior command responsibility. Whether I say 7(1), it's individual criminal responsibility. The charge of complicity of genocide, and genocide, has now been removed from the consolidated amended indictment for the same reasons as those of your colleagues. The initial indictment did not charge you with genocide under Article 4(3)(a). Count 1 of the consolidated amended indictment, however, charges you with genocide, punishable under Articles 4(3)(a) and 7(1) but limited to aiding and abetting genocide. And also under Article 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal; that is, in your capacity as a superior. In regard to Count 2, conspiracy to commit genocide, as is -- it appears in the consolidated amended indictment, while your name and this -- please, Prosecution, also please note. While your name does not appear above paragraph 34 and in paragraphs 34 and 35 that relate to Count 2, your name does appear on the first page of the consolidated amended indictment as one of the accused charged with genocide and conspiracy to commit genocide. The Prosecution has requested, in its response to the Defence motions under Rule 72 to add your name where it is missing in the paragraphs that relate to Count 2, in order to clarify that you are charged with conspiracy to commit genocide. Accordingly, you are going to be asked to plead to the charge in Count 2, that is conspiracy to commit genocide. In the initial indictment, you were also charged with persecutions, which included the forcible transfer of Bosnian Muslims from the Srebrenica enclave. In the consolidated amended indictment, the charge of forcible transfer not only applies to women and children but also to the forced bussing of the men separated at Potocari or captured or having surrendered from the column of people fleeing in the Srebrenica enclave up to the Zvornik area where they were ultimately captured and executed. This is not according to me; it's according to the Prosecution. It stands to be proven. In addition, the consolidated amended indictment charges the forcible transfer of the Bosnian Muslim population from the Zepa enclave, including the deportation of the men from Zepa. Accordingly, the charges of persecution have been extended and a charge of deportation has been added. Have I been clear to you, Mr. Borovcanin? Have you been able to follow?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BOROVCANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. You may remain standing now. I am now going through the various counts one by one, and the first count charges you with genocide punishable under 4(3)(a) and 7(1), it's Articles of the Statute, limited to aiding and abetting genocide, and Article 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you wish to plead to --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BOROVCANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation], Your Honour, I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Count 2 charges you with conspiracy to commit genocide, punishable under Articles 4(3)(b) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you wish to plead to this Article 2 -- Count 2?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BOROVCANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, before I enter my plea, may I say something in relation to that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BOROVCANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The indictment that I received, the last indictment that I received does not mention my name in Count 2. In the contents of Count 2 my name does not appear. My name figures in the title of the indictment together with others as charged with Count 2. Later it was explained to me that it was a technical mistake, a clerical error, so it appears to me that it is more likely that the clerical error would be with respect to the title. I find it hard to see why I do not appear later on. I would like to ask my counsel to explain what the situation is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. By all means. I thank you for expressing your concerns, Mr. Borovcanin. In the meantime, while this is being discussed, you may remain seated. Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, the first mention of adding new charges against Mr. Borovcanin, Count 2, and I speak about Count 2 of the indictment, was on Prosecutor's submission dated January 21st. So it wasn't in the indictment that my client received dating from November 11. And in its submission, it's a reply that the Prosecution filed of January 21st. The Prosecution asked for leave to amend the indictment by adding the name of Mr. Borovcanin in Count 2 of the indictment, and there is no ruling on this request of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I think I -- do you want to respond to that, Mr. McCloskey? Because it's not exactly how you put it. The submission is that your client is there from the 11th -- is there. He is mentioned but he's not mentioned specifically everywhere that he should have been mentioned. This is the position. But that is the mistake. The mistake does not consist from what I could understand that he has been erroneously mentioned somewhere when he shouldn't have been mentioned. The submission is that he should have been mentioned more and was not mentioned but there should be no doubt left in the minds of whoever that he is included in the charge of conspiracy to commit genocide. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think you've got it correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this is the position. I mean -- Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can understand your position. However, the motion seeking for leave to amend the indictment filed by the Prosecution before the amended indictment was filed in November does not contain the name of Mr. Borovcanin for Count 2. There is absolutely no explanation regarding Mr. Borovcanin's involvement in complicity to commit genocide.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, the amended indictment, in its very first page, starts with a declaration that the Prosecution, pursuant to her authority -- the Prosecutor, pursuant to her authority, et cetera, charges, amongst others, your client with genocide, conspiracy to commit genocide. So this does not leave any doubt in the minds of anyone that that is what the consolidated amended indictment seeks to -- seeks to confirm. As happens in many instances, mistakes result in all indictments. It seems that in Count 2, when it comes to paragraph 34, his name is missing, as you said. But the Prosecution is not giving an explanation to the effect that there was a mistake in the first page his name should have never appeared together with the others as being charged with conspiracy to commit genocide. What they are explaining is that the mistake happened in the description or in the listing of names in paragraphs 34 and 35; namely, that his name should have appeared there as -- there as well. It's true that that has not been decided. I mean, I am not in any way suggesting that it has been decided, but I think the safest way of going about it is to ask him to enter the plea today because I think it will be harbouring a little bit of -- bring a little bit of an illusion to think that it's exactly the opposite way around. And especially if you look at some of the paragraphs preceding 34, particularly 33, it is indicative that destruction of women, children, et cetera, it was never apparent from the indictment that it was the intention of the Prosecution to leave your client out from -- especially considering the way he was accused under the initial indictment in the first place. So I don't think I should say more than that. I am going to proceed with asking you whether you wish to plead guilty or not guilty to Count 2. I explained to you what the circumstances are. If you want the opportunity to consult with your lawyer --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is precisely what I wanted to ask, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So what I suggest, I don't know what instructions, security officers, what instructions you may have on this. I would like him to grant him a moment to consult with his counsel. Do you prefer to have the consultation in the courtroom, here, somewhere in the corner or outside?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I think it would be fine with us to consult in the courtroom. We don't need any extra space.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I tell you what to do because we are soon over in any case. We'll have a short break during which you will have an opportunity to consult with your client on this. And then we will proceed with the entering of pleas later. We'll have -- if I have the indulgence of the staff, how much time do you wish to have? I reckon that we only have about 20 minutes more of sitting, or half an hour at the moment -- at best. I can't see -- I can't see anyone behind the dark glasses. 15 minutes? Yeah, 15 minutes break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, have you conferred with your client?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can confirm that I consulted with my client. What I have to say is that earlier this morning when I met Mr. Borovcanin in the detention unit and when we discussed the issue of his plea, it seems that he was -- that the indictment that we are discussing about didn't contain his name in count -- is in these counts. So it is our position, I have to say it's my position, Mr. Stojanovic position, and also Mr. Borovcanin's position, that it would be better for him not to plead on this count of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Do you confirm, Mr. Borovcanin, please stand up, on Count 2, do you confirm the position as explained by your lawyer now; in other words, that you are not entering a plea on Count 2?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BOROVCANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. My reaction to that is that there is a 30-day grace period which becomes applicable. If at the end of 30 days you do not enter a plea, then I will enter a plea of not guilty on your behalf. For that purpose, Mr. Von Hebel, there will be a further Status Conference for accused Borovcanin alone, 30 days from now, unless he signifies his intention to enter a plea earlier. Count 3 charges you with extermination. This is a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 3(b), 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute. How do you wish to plead? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BOROVCANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Count 4 charges you with murder, as a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(a), 7(1) and also 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you wish to plead? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BOROVCANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Count 4 charges you with the same crime, murder, but this time being a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Articles 3, 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you wish to plead? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BOROVCANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Count 6 charges you with persecutions on political, racial and religious grounds, a crime against humanity, which includes murder, cruel and inhumane treatment, terrorising the civilian population, destruction of personal property and forcible transfer, punishable under Articles 5(h), 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you wish to plead? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BOROVCANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Count 7 charges you with inhumane acts, being forcible transfer. This is a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(i), 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of this Tribunal. How do you wish to plead? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BOROVCANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Borovcanin, Count 8, finally, charges you with deportation, being a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(d), 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of this Tribunal. How do you wish to plead? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BOROVCANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Mr. Borovcanin. You may sit down. And, Madam Registrar, please enter that Mr. Borovcanin has entered a plea of not guilty on all counts except Count 2, to which he has not entered a plea. I now come to you, Mr. Pandurevic. You may remain seated for the time being. I will tell you when to rise. Yours is less complicated. In the initial indictment, you were charged with conspiracy to commit genocide, contrary to or in violation of Articles 4(3)(b) and 7(1) of the Statute. In other words, you are charged with individual criminal responsibility in relation to this crime. The situation has now changed. The consolidated amended indictment also charges you with -- under 7(3), Article 7(3) of the Statute, that is with command responsibility for conspiracy to commit genocide. Second point is the following: In the initial indictment you were charged with persecutions and which included forcible -- the forcible transfer of Bosnian Muslims from the Srebrenica enclave. The situation has changed somewhat. In the consolidated amended indictment, the charge of forcible transfer does not -- not only applies -- not only applies to the women and children but it extends also to the bussing, forced bussing, of men who, according to the Prosecution, were separated at Potocari or captured or having surrendered from the column of people fleeing the Srebrenica enclave up to the Zvornik area, where they were, according to the Prosecution, ultimately executed. In addition, the consolidated amended indictment charges the forceable transfer of Bosnian Muslim population from the Zepa enclave, including the deportation of the men from Zepa. Accordingly, you will find that in the consolidated amended indictment, the charge of persecutions has been extended and a charge of deportation has been added. Lastly, by contrast to the initial indictment, the consolidated amended indictment also explicitly charges you as one of the participants in a joint criminal enterprise to forcibly transfer the Bosnian Muslim population and to commit the mass killings. These are basically the main differences that there are. Now I ask you to stand up, please. I will go through the counts one by one and we'll ask you to enter a plea. Please stand up. Mr. Pandurevic, the first Count against you is one of genocide, punishable under Articles 4(3)(a), 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute of this Tribunal. How do you wish to plead? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PANDUREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Count 2 charges you with conspiracy to commit genocide, punishable under Articles 4(3)(b), 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute. How do you wish to plead? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PANDUREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Count 3 charges with you extermination as being a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(b), 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute. How do you wish to plead? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PANDUREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Count 4 charges you with murder being a crime against humanity punishable under Articles 5(a), 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute. How do you wish to plead? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PANDUREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Count five charges you with murder a violation of the laws or customs of war punishable under Articles 3, 7(1), 7(3) of the Statute. How do you wish to plead? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PANDUREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Count 6 charges you with persecutions on political, racial, and religious grounds, a crime against humanity including murder, cruel and inhumane treatment, terrorising a civilian population, destruction of personal property and forcible transfer, punishable under Articles 5(h), 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute. How do you wish to plead? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PANDUREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Count 7 charges you with inhumane acts being forcible transfer, against -- a crime against humanity punishable under Articles 5(i) 7(1), 7(3) of the Statute. How do you wish to plead? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PANDUREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And finally Count 8 charges you with deportation. As I have explained already, this is a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(d), 7(1), 7(3). How do you wish to plead? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PANDUREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Pandurevic. You may sit down. And for the record, Ms. Fabian, please enter that Mr. Pandurevic has pleaded not guilty to all eight counts. And I finally come to you, Mr. Trbic. Yours is even more simple than that of the others. In the initial indictment, you were charged with one count, that is murder, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(a) and 7(1) of the Statute. This charge remains now in the consolidated amended indictment as Count 4. In addition, however, the consolidated indictment now charges you with genocide, conspiracy to commit genocide, extermination, murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war, persecutions, inhumane acts, and deportation. By contrast to the initial indictment, the consolidated indictment -- amended indictment also explicitly charges you as one of the participants in a joint criminal enterprise to forcibly transfer the Bosnian Muslim population and to commit the mass killings. Mr. Trbic, could you stand up, please? I'm going to ask you whether you wish to enter a plea in which case you tell me either guilty or not guilty. Count 1 charges you with genocide, punishable under Articles 4(3)(a) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you wish to plead? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED TRBIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Count 2 charges you with conspiracy to commit genocide, punishable Articles 4(3)(b) and 7(1) of the Statute. How do you wish to plead? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED TRBIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Count 3 charges you with extermination, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(b) and 7(1) of the Statute. How do you wish to plead? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED TRBIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Count 4 charges you with murder a crime against humanity punishable under Articles 5(a) and 7(1) of the statute. How do you wish to plead? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED TRBIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Count 5 charges you also with murder, this time being a violations of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute. How do you wish to plead? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED TRBIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Count 6 charges you with persecutions on political, racial and religious grounds, a crime against humanity, including murder, cruel and inhumane treatment, terrorising the civilian population, destruction of personal property and forcible transfer, punishable under Articles 5(h) and 7(1) of the Statute. How do you plead? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED TRBIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Count 7 charges you with inhumane acts forcible transfer, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(i) and 7(1) of the Statute. How do you wish to plead? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED TRBIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And finally Count 8 charges you with deportation, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(d) and 7(1) of the Statute. How do you plead? Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED TRBIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Trbic. You may sit down and Madam Registrar, could you please enter a record to the effect that Mr. Trbic has entered a plea of not guilty to all eight counts. I thank you all. And I now come to work plan for this trial. And I'm doing this because I am, of course, required to do so by Rule 65 ter(D)(ii). I have been informed by Mr. Von Hebel that what will happen between now and when we start the trial and when the trial will start has been subject of some debate during the 65 ter Conferences of the 6th of March and of yesterday. And Mr. Von Hebel has more or less provided me with a revised plan which will, of course, be revised as -- and if necessary, because in these cases obviously things happen and dates have to shift. I have actually taken note of all the submissions that you have both made to Mr. Von Hebel, and as I said, although in my mind I do have a plan, the work plan may shift as a result of developments. But this should not in any way keep us from trying to plan as accurately as we can, and establish a target date for the conclusion of the pre-trial stage and commencement of the trial. In my calculations, and again I say this subject, of course, to possible revisions, even in my mind, of my calculations, I think that we should be in the position, and I can expect all parties to be ready for trial practically immediately after the summer recess. That's my opinion. But I also advised that it will be probably wiser to make an allowance for an extra week or two at the most, to cover any possible contingencies that we may encounter in the meantime and also to make sure that every one of you is given all the opportunities necessary to present the pre-trial Chamber with all the documentation that we require from you. There are some things to which I give priority. Obviously, the first thing that must be done, and which depends on me rather than on you, is to come forward with a final decision on all the motions that relate to the indictment. I'm fully aware that until and unless that becomes final, there is no point in asking you particularly to come forward with a response in relation to agreed facts, to any possible motion on adjudicated facts, Rule 92 bis motions, and so on and so forth. I fully concur, agree, and I say it openly, that what must happen first is our decision. But from the moment our decision becomes public, is handed down, in other words, we need to start working. So what I am suggesting is that while I, together with the other two judges and our staff, work on the decision that I have just mentioned, the Prosecution tries to work on the following. We have agreed that we need to address the pre-trial Prosecution brief. Do you have a definitive date in mind where you will certainly be in a position to give us that, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We were -- had obligated ourselves to the 21st of April. As we get closer and actually looking at our draft and being slightly delayed by the Stakic judgement, if we could get one more week, I think we would give you a better product so we would be asking for a one week extension to our own initial deadline of April 21, to 28 April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I had in mind -- I will grant you that, Mr. McCloskey, without much further discussion. I had in mind, then, that within a week from the filing of the pre-trial Prosecution brief, you file an adjudicated facts proposal, a proper motion. That would have been the 28 April, we now have to shift it by one week. Can anyone tell me the -- 5th May? 5th May. That would be the 5th May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That looks good for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I had in mind the 12th of May for Rule 92 bis motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That looks good as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll leave it at 12th? And you indicated that by the 9th of June you should be in a position to submit Mr. Butler's, the military expert, report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are aware, Mr. McCloskey, of Mr. Miletic's motions, two motions, in relation to the translation of the proposed adjudicated facts and Rule 92 bis motion. Do you think that you would spare the Trial Chamber the trouble of having to decide that by having recourse to your translation resources in the OTP and have those two motions translated into B/C/S. For that, I would be prepared to extend the dates of the 5th of May and the 12th of May by another week.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The 92 bis statements of the witnesses are in B/C/S. Many of them, as you know, were from prior testimony and the Defence should have had the audio of that in B/C/S and hopefully now the capability to listen to the audio, which is actually I think the best way for them to have it given the enormous resources it would be to do it otherwise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the adjudicated facts?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The adjudicated facts --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is included too in Madam Fauveau's motion. I've seen others in other cases and also in my case, so we are not -- I think we are talking of a document which may be translated in two or three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Something that simple, I will endeavour to talk to CLSS about. They always try to be cooperative but as you know they are very honest about their abilities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And I know what burden they carry as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So we'll check with them on that. On the adjudicated facts we had sent out a potential agreed facts to the Accused and we were hoping to get some response on that to perhaps reduce the burden of the adjudicated facts. Unfortunately we haven't heard much on that so our burden has not been reduced and so we will be able to go forward without any help from the Accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But agreed facts and adjudicated facts are not the same thing. It should never be put in the same basket. I mean there are definitely adjudicated facts to which the Defence can agree, but the two -- the two are not the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No. My only point is, as you said, if the Defence agreed to some fact that had already been adjudicated, the motion would be a little lighter on that but -- and some facts have been, as you know so adjudicated here that we were hoping to get some response but there are eight accused and we are being realistic. That would be a hard thing to imagine getting too many people agree, so we are ready to go forward with the adjudicated facts motion as we said and we will try to get that deal with CLSS about how to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So the position is as follows: If in relation to adjudicated facts and Rule 92 bis motion, you are in a position or you agree -- I mean, I'm no way forcing you or asking to do this I'm just inviting you to consider this possibility, if you are prepared to have B/C/S version accompany the original motion, then you can take the two dates that I indicated to you, the 5th of May and 12th of May respectively extended by another week in each case. If not, they will remain firm. In other words, adjudicated facts, 5th of May, and Rule 92 bis motion, 12th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have that in B/C/S and we have some in French if anyone cares to see them in French.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.
