Starting now, from the date when we will hand down the decision on the form of the indictment, the Defence -- when I say the Defence, it means each and every team will have three weeks within which to come forward with any notification of alibi or any special defence in terms of Rule 67(A). You will recall that this -- there have already been some orders and I agreed that it makes much more sense to wait until the decision on the form of the indictment, which is not really the right medicine but I agree that it's wiser to wait until that matter is decided and then we will deal with the rest. So Defence notification of alibi or any special defence under Rule 67 not later than three weeks from the date of the Trial Chamber's decision on the form of the indictment. Any motion or remarks or official position that you would desire to take in relation to agreed facts, proposed adjudicated facts, and Rule 92 bis motion, you will need to address by not later than one month from the date of the decision of the Trial Chamber on the form of the indictment. As it is, and as the situation would be or is expected to be, at that point in time, but depending, of course, on how things work out, my idea is that each one of the Defence teams should have their pre-trial brief filed by not later than the 14th of July. That's when we go basically on recess, more or less on recess. So it's important that we have all these before we go on recess. Then I plan either during the recess or immediately after the recess, or towards the end of the recess, I plan to have the full Trial Chamber here in The Hague. We would require some refreshing training on the e-system which we will be using for the trial. Maybe if anyone of you also needs some coaching, some training, you will let me know and I will attend to that. And I plan to start the case round about, if not exactly, on the 21st of August. That's my plan. We can shift by one week or two weeks, as I explained earlier but, please, let's all try to get started. Basically what I'm saying is this that would be almost naive on my part to expect that the road ahead will be full of roses and no problems and no thorns, no appeals, and no this and no that. So with that in mind, with that in mind, and with the responsibility also in mind, the responsibility that I have, I am going to try to start at the earliest opportunity. According to me, the earliest ideally would be the 21st of August. But I may be too optimistic and I'm fully aware that we may need another week or two before we could actually start. We would start with the -- my intention would be that towards the end of August or between the 21st at any time before the end of August we will have the Pre-Trial Conference, to be followed a week after by the opening statements and the start of the trial, so basically, as I envisage it, if there is a one-week delay, the Pre-Trial Conference will take place on the 28th of August, with the trial starting a week after. If there is a two-week delay, the Pre-Trial Conference will be on the -- seven days after the 28th of August, and then we start the week after with the opening statements, to be followed by what we discussed in private session. Do you read me? To be followed then by that. So basically there will be that also breathing space, further breathing space, for you to -- there is a possibility, at least I have that indication, that some of the time between now and when we start the trial may be made use of, profitably made use of for receiving testimony in the forms provided for under the Rules. I have to -- still to think about that. If that matter comes up, if and when, but if it is at all possible then, of course, after hearing what you have to say we will decide accordingly but that's the position for the time being. I have said what I have said to give you an indication of what my intentions are. We all have lived pre-trials and trials before in our lives. Some more than others. And you would agree with me and I would agree with you that you can never -- at this stage you can never be that sure as to the exact date when we will start the trial but more or less that's what I am aiming at, all right? There are a few final things that I would like to address. In anticipation of all this, and also to be able to plan ahead better, I would like the Defence teams to discuss amongst themselves the way they wish to proceed in relation to the opening -- Defence opening statements. There may be some who may wish to make an opening statement. There may be others who may not wish to make opening statements. There may be controversies amongst you as to who should go first, who should go second, and who should go after and last. I will, of course, not interfere in all this. But please don't allow a situation to obtain where we come to the day when we are supposed to hear the first of the Defence opening statements, if there will be any, and Trial Chamber would not be in a position even to know if there is going to be one, who is going to go first, who is going to go second, et cetera. This is a big trial. There are eight defence teams. I appeal to your cooperation. And I will accommodate you accordingly, but you need to discuss this amongst yourselves because there may be conflicting interests, or there may be some who would not wish to make any opening statement. Also, although, of course, the situation -- I realise that the situation may change between now and when we start the trial, I suppose you ought to start consulting with your clients whether they too would like to make any statements at the beginning of the trial. In which case, please do let us know because we will need to plan accordingly. All right? Now, I am going to ask each one of you the usual questions about your state of detention, your state of health, be it mental or physical. I'll start with you, Mr. Popovic. I will keep the same order, Mr. Popovic, Mr. Beara; we'll go in that order. Mr. Popovic, and if there is any one of you who would like to address me on any of these matters, particularly health matters, in private session, closed session, in other words, keep it away from the public, please do let me know straight away. Mr. Popovic, I would like to know if you have anything to tell me in relation to the conditions of your detention or in relation to your health or anything else that, in your opinion, I should be made aware of.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the time being, Your Honour, I don't have any complaints. I think everything is in order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Mr. Popovic. Please be seated. Mr. Beara. The same question to you. If there is anything that you would like to bring to my notice in public or in private.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BEARA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I don't have anything in particular. The detention -- the conditions of my detention are excellent and my health is also very good. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm happy to hear that, Mr. Beara. I thank you so much. Mr. Drago Nikolic. The same question to you, your feedback on your conditions of detention and on the state of your health or any other matter that you would like to address me upon in public or in private.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone for the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please start again.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I do not have any complaints as to the conditions of my detention, and my health is equally good. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Nikolic. Mr. Borovcanin. The same question to you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BOROVCANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, as far as my health is concerned, I do not have any problems whatsoever. As for the conditions of my detention, I don't think I have anything to add in relation to what you already know. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Borovcanin. Mr. Miletic is not here. Mr. Gvero is not here. Mr. Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PANDUREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, thank you for your concern. My health is good, and the conditions of my detention are also good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you, Mr. Pandurevic. Mr. Trbic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED TRBIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No complaints whatsoever, Your Honour. Thank you for asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Trbic. You may sit down. So, now, any other matter that the parties would like to address? I see Mr. Bourgon anxiously waiting to be heard. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. Good afternoon, Your Honour. I rise at this point to address the -- on behalf of my colleagues representing the eight accused in this courtroom, or at least eight co-accused in these proceedings, regarding our ability to be ready for trial at a certain date, and in this respect I would like to make five observations. My first observation as a preliminary matter is I would like to express on behalf of my colleagues our appreciation for your involvement leading to this case being ranked at level 3 by the Registry. We believe that this is directly related to the issue of setting an appropriate date for beginning this trial. My second observation is that on the 6th of March, when we had the Rule 65 ter meeting with the Senior Legal Officer, I indicated that as a consequence of having this trial ranked at level 3, all Defence teams had increased their rate of preparation, and we all agree that we can be ready to begin this trial by 1 November of this year. Follows my third observation. Of course, if the Trial Chamber decides, or should the Trial Chamber decide on an earlier date, it goes without saying that all Defence teams will be present and will be there for trial. However, we are collectively of the view that this is likely to cause longer delays than the time which we could save by starting earlier considering a number of issues, such as, for example, potential requests for short term adjournments at a time when witnesses are present in The Hague, which could be counterproductive, and also this will impact on the ability of Defence to work with, to work on, and meet with the Prosecution with the aim of possibly agreeing on stipulations which could shorten the trial. My fourth and last observation is that there is another related issue that goes with starting the trial on 1 November. And this is an issue which is of significant importance to all Defence teams, and this is also an issue which I raised yesterday during the Rule 65 ter meeting with the Senior Legal Officer. And this issue is that of the possibility of a long-term postponement in the beginning of this trial in the event the Prosecution requests that a further accused be joined to the proceedings between now and the beginning of the trial. The consequences of such an event must be mentioned, and we believe it is necessary to bring these consequences to your attention, Your Honour. First, in order to be ready for November, we have, of course, increased the rate of our preparations, but the consequence will be that when we reach the beginning of the trial, with a view to being ready, and working along with the Trial Chamber, we will have exhausted all resources at our disposal between now and the day which will be decided upon by the Trial Chamber. Accordingly, taking, for example, for the sake of this submission, that a further accused was joined to this -- to these, the present proceedings, by the Prosecution, by way of motion, of course, requesting that this is what the Prosecution would like, it means that from that point on, the Defence will have no more resources, whereas significant resources would be required to allow the Defence to do a number of things, such as, one, to keep up with the Prosecution during that postponement or adjournment, in order to simply keep up with the work taking place within the Office of the Prosecutor. Two, to work, investigate and adjust the case for the Defence for each of the respective accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me one second. I'm sorry to interrupt. If we are going to get into any subjects of a speculative nature like this, could we go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't see the need, but if it puts your mind at rest, let's go into private session. I mean, this is all speculation for the time being. I understand exactly what he means. Some people might not understand. Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. In conclusion, all Defence teams in this case, and I speak here this behalf of all my colleagues are more than willing to work with yourself as the Pre-Trial Judge and with the Trial Chamber to which this case will be assigned for trial to ensure that this trial can begin at the earliest possibility and without delay. That being said, given the work that we still have to do to be ready for trial, we are of the view that a realistic date to which we agree to be bound by would be 1 November. Just to name one further example of the things that are happening for which additional time is required is what is happening today in the war crimes chamber in Sarajevo. The war crimes chamber is increasing its pace of work. Many people are being either brought for investigation, trials are about to take place, and there will be a lot of evidence which will be generated by the war crimes chamber in Sarajevo which the Defence needs to be aware of, needs to review, before we can proceed soundly with this trial. This is just to name one example. That being said, Your Honour, we all want to begin at the earliest possibility but there is some level of uncertainty here, and all Defence counsel believe it was necessary at least to bring these issues to your attention so that we know what we are getting into and also to understand -- to underline the need for a firm date. You are not giving us a firm date. We believe this firm date should be adjusted to 1 November but we will be -- we will respect, of course, any date set by the Trial Chamber, but we will work accordingly and spend our resources according with the date that you give us with, of course, the consequences that might arise. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Are there any matters that the Prosecution would like to address?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So I think we can safely adjourn now. As to the matters that you raised, Mr. Bourgon, of course, they will receive my full attention as well as that of my two colleagues, present and future. As to the rest, if the situation changes, as you tried to speculate, then obviously I will not speculate now but obviously you will hear from me and I will need to hear from you and any problems that you indeed will face will be addressed and where needed you will find my support. But let's plan according to what we have here and not what could possibly happen which might not happen. If that happens, we are obviously not starting in August and not starting in November. The case is adjourned.
